title: Transparent Admission Proxy for Cost-Aware Load Shedding and Degraded Responses
creator: Maya Chen
description: We need a low-latency admission-layer that performs inexpensive request-cost estimation and applies transparent, policy-driven degradation before requests enter the serving runtime. The goal is to reduce emergency load-shedding pain by shifting decisions earlier: classify request cost, apply safe transformations (prompt trims, structured defaults, early exits), and route or reject according to multi-region SLO budgets and circuit-breaker state. This ticket scopes a prototype (proxy + policy engine) and a canary plan for integrating with runtime admission and Console visibility.
implementation_notes: Build a lightweight gRPC/HTTP proxy that attaches before the main router to observe full request envelope and client SLO metadata
Implement a cost estimator (fast heuristics) that predicts token cost, KV-cache hit probability, and predicted latency band
Define degradation transforms: short_prompt_trim, system_prompt_summarize, context_window_prune, structured-defaults, partial-response-early-return
Policy engine evaluates: tenant quotas, per-region headroom, circuit-breaker state, model-variant fallback and configured grace levels
Expose decisions and metrics to Console: per-request decision tag, estimated cost, transform applied, accepted/denied reason
Integrate with existing circuit breaker service (topic ENG-90321) and multi-region failover coordinator (ENG-14567) for unified actions
Add end-to-end tests for correctness of transformations and false-positive rejection rate <0.5% for synthetic traffic
Plan gradual rollout: internal canary (10% traffic) -> beta tenants -> global rollout with throttled window and rollback hooks
acceptance_criteria: Proxy latency (p50) < 2ms added to request path in production under typical load
Proxy correctly classifies >90% of high-cost requests (precision) in offline eval with historical traces
Transformation correctness: trimmed prompts preserve structured intents for 95% of test prompts
Console shows per-route decision telemetry and aggregated cost-savings dashboard for the canary cohort
Canary run demonstrates >=15% reduction in emergency shedding incidents in target region under spike tests
Security checklist completed: no plaintext credential leakage, KMS-integrated audit for decision logs
Operator runbook updated with rollback and escalation steps and SLO adjustments
comments: 2026-03-10 Maya Chen: Initial write-up and scope. This arose from recurring incidents where runtime had to drop entire priority lanes during cross-region spike; we can avoid many by trimming earlier.

2026-03-11 Luca Patel: Spike-prototype started. Implemented estimator heuristic using token count, prompt complexity score, and user hint header. Early results on 1M historical requests: estimator AUC 0.87.
2026-03-12 Design review (A. Rivera): Suggested 'preserve-contract' transform that guarantees function-call signatures remain intact; required for customers using structured outputs.
2026-03-13 SRE (T. Nguyen): Raised concern about added attack surface. We'll restrict proxy to authenticated internal routes, enforce mTLS, and rate-limit control-plane calls.
2026-03-14 PM (R. Ortiz): Prioritize Console UX for auditability. Add a per-tenant view for decisions and an exportable CSV for customer support.
